replacement: Alyosha was heading across the cathedral square to the widow Morozov’s house, to see Grushenka. She had sent Fenya to him early that morning with an urgent message asking him to come. Fenya told him, when he questioned her, that her mistress had been particularly upset since the day before. In the two months since Mitya’s arrest, Alyosha had often visited the widow Morozov’s house, partly because he wished to and partly to carry messages for Mitya. Three days after Mitya was arrested, Grushenka had fallen gravely ill, and she remained ill for almost five weeks. For one whole week she had lain unconscious. She had changed a great deal. She was thinner and a little sallow, although for the last fortnight she had been well enough to go out. Yet to Alyosha her face was more attractive than ever, and he liked meeting her eyes when he came in. Her face had taken on a look of firmness and intelligent purpose. There were signs in her of a spiritual transformation, and one could see a steadfast, fine, humble determination that nothing could shake. A small vertical line had appeared between her brows, and at first glance it gave her charming face a thoughtful, almost stern look. Hardly a trace remained of her old frivolity.
